mainEntity.name: When is the individual tax return deadline in Australia?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you lodge your own return, the deadline is 31 October each year. Using a registered tax agent generally extends the deadline — often to 15 May the following year — provided you are registered with the agent before 31 October. We match you with a vetted local agent so you get the extended deadline.

Quarterly BAS is generally due on the 28th of the month after the quarter ends — 28 July, 28 October, 28 January and 28 April. Monthly BAS is due on the 21st of the following month. Registered agents often receive extended lodgement dates. Tell us your BAS cycle and we will match you with a local agent who lodges on time.

With the introduction of Payday Super from 1 July 2026, employers must pay super guarantee each payday. The contributions must reach the employee's super fund within 7 business days of payday. Missing SG deadlines triggers the super guarantee charge and, for company directors, personal director penalty notices.

mainEntity.name: What is Payday Super and when does it start?

acceptedAnswer.text: From 1 July 2026, employers must pay super guarantee contributions alongside each payday, with contributions required to reach the employee's fund within 7 business days — which replaced the former quarterly cycle. A matched accountant ensures your payroll system is ready so you meet every payday deadline.

mainEntity.name: When do company and trust tax returns need to be lodged?

acceptedAnswer.text: Company and trust returns are generally due by 15 January — or later if a registered agent lodges on your behalf. Trust distribution resolutions should be made by 30 June each year to be valid. Companies also face ASIC annual review deadlines. We match you with a local accountant who manages all of these.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I lodge my tax return or BAS late?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ATO may apply a failure-to-lodge (FTL) penalty and, where tax is payable, general interest charge (GIC) on the outstanding amount. Persistent non-lodgement can lead to a default assessment or stronger recovery action. Engaging a registered agent early — and using their extended deadlines — minimises the risk.

mainEntity.name: What should I do before 30 June (EOFY)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Super contributions within your cap, pre-paid expenses, stock write-offs, bad-debt settlements and trust distribution resolutions all need to happen before 30 June to count in the current financial year. A matched accountant reviews your position in May or June and flags the actions worth taking — so you reduce tax rather than react after year-end.

mainEntity.name: How do I get matched with an accountant to stay on time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Complete our 60-second questionnaire with your postcode and needs. We match you with a vetted local accountant whose services fit your situation — individual returns, BAS, super, company or trust — so you meet every deadline. The matching is free with no obligation.

VB WRITTEN BY Vic Bulfone Founder, Your Accountant Match LAST REVIEWED 29 September 2026 Last verified against ATO guidance 29 September 2026 TAX DATES GUIDE Key Tax Deadlines for Australians Personal tax return deadlines If you lodge your own individual tax return, the deadline is 31 October each year. If you use a registered tax agent, you generally receive an extended lodgement deadline — often as late as May the following year, provided you are on the agent's lodgement program before 31 October. That extended deadline is one of the clearest reasons to engage an agent rather than self-lodge. Late lodgement can trigger a failure-to-lodge (FTL) penalty and, where tax is payable, general interest charge (GIC) on the outstanding amount. Business & BAS due dates If you are registered for GST, you lodge a Business Activity Statement (BAS). Quarterly BAS is generally due on the 28th of the month after the quarter ends — so 28 July, 28 October, 28 January and 28 April. Monthly BAS is due on the 21st of the following month. Registered agents often receive extended BAS lodgement dates. PAYG instalments and income tax instalments are reported through the BAS as well. Late BAS attracts FTL penalties and interest on any net amount payable. Superannuation (SG) cutoffs With the introduction of Payday Super from 1 July 2026, employers must pay super guarantee each payday. The contributions must reach the employee's super fund within 7 business days of payday. For SMSF members, personal contributions must be received by 28 January and 28 July to count toward each half-year's cap. Missing SG deadlines triggers the super guarantee charge (SGC) and, for company directors, personal director penalty notices. Company, trust & partnership deadlines Companies, trusts and partnerships lodge their own tax returns, separate from the individuals behind them. Company and trust returns are generally due by 15 January (or later if a registered agent lodges on your behalf). Trust distribution resolutions should be made by 30 June each year — before year-end — to be valid. Companies also face ASIC annual review fees and lodgement deadlines. Directors remain personally liable for unpaid PAYG withholding and super guarantee, so staying on time matters. Key 30 June (EOFY) actions A number of tax-effective moves must happen before 30 June to count in the current financial year: making super contributions within your cap, pre-paying expenses, writing off obsolete stock, settling bad debts, and documenting trust distribution resolutions. After 30 June those opportunities close for that year. A matched accountant reviews your position in May or June and flags the actions worth taking before year-end — proactive planning that reduces tax rather than reacting after the fact.
